The text says a person "may be presumed innocent" on a day if there is no conviction of that person happening no later than that day. Ana's conviction happens on 5 January 2027, so on that day the condition (no conviction at or before that day) fails. The text therefore grants no permission for that day. It says only that the permission holds when the condition is met, and it does not say what holds otherwise, so it does not say whether presumption is required or forbidden. "Not required" doesn't follow from a permission alone either, but the best match is that the permission is absent and the text is silent on the rest.

Among the options, C says it is not required and the text is silent on whether it is forbidden. D says it is permitted, which is wrong because the condition fails. E says the text says nothing about it on that day, which fits since the text only states a sufficient condition for permission and nothing for the case where the condition fails.

Reading "may be presumed innocent … if [condition]" as a conditional permission, the text gives no permission here but also does not forbid anything. E is the most accurate.

ANSWER: E
